about: REQ-356 — what every new site plan starts with.
DATA AND NOT CODE, so the list can change without a code change. The decisions
are [[DOC-64]] §6 and the standing checks are §7; this file is that document's
two tables, in the shape the plan stores them. A plan is seeded once, when it is
first written, so editing this file changes plans created afterwards and leaves
`settle` is how the decision is expected to be settled — asked, talked through,
shown, or offered ([[DOC-64]] §3.1). It tells the coordinator how to raise it.
`triggers` name the moments a check fires ([[DOC-64]] §7). Firing them is the
coordinator's runtime and out of scope here; the names are recorded so that
runtime has something to match on.
[[REQ-379]] — `feature_catalogue` is the fixed list a site's features are
chosen from, in the client's words, and `asks` are the panel questions a new
plan starts with. The one seeded ask is the features ask: its options are the
catalogue (`options_from`), so the catalogue is stated once. Answering it fills
the plan's `functionality`, which is what gives "are we done?" something to
be measured against. A feature outside the catalogue can still be recorded
with `set_feature`; the catalogue is what the client is offered, not a limit.

asks.prompt: Which of these does your site need?
asks.why: So we build what you need and can tell when the site is finished.

decisions.title: Goal, and how we'd know (measure or proxy)
Quality bar, in the client's words
Call to action: what we want the visitor to do
Core story: what the visitor should take away
Layout system (grid, rhythm, how sections hold together)
Image supply: what the client has, and whether it's usable
Animation approach ("none" is a valid answer)

checks.question: Are we all happy with the layout?
You said [quality bar]. Does this meet it?
[Concept decision] is still a default. Want to see alternatives?
Before we build the other pages: are voice and layout settled?
Have we looked at it on a phone?
How does it feel to scroll through?
Ready to publish? Links, contact routing, share card, favicon
